text:
ops-bot: ALERT: realtime latency regression detected for prod cluster us-west-2 route /v1/stream. p95 jumped from ~780ms -> ~2.4s, p99 ~1.2s -> ~5.6s. Streaming stalls and some client-side timeouts observed. Paging on-call @alice :rotating_light:
alice: I'm on-call, ack. Starting triage. Who's on infra? @bob?
bob: I can join. grabbing dashboards now.
metrics-bot: Snapshot: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/streaming/latency?orgId=1&refresh=now - p95/p99 graphs + request rate.
carol: I see a correlated increase in long-running KV cache reads on the runtime (kv_hit_ratio dip, active KV size up). Could be cache growth from long chat sessions.
dave: Also seeing GPU queue depth spike on pool-a100-usw2, queue_wait p95 ~820ms. Possible request bursting + batching mismatch.
alice: ok hypothesis: KV cache growth -> longer KV loads -> runtime scheduling pressure -> GPU queueing -> tail latency.
alice: quick checks: 1) confirm recent rollout? 2) check model variants, 3) check autoscaler and pod restarts.
carol: no model rollout in last 24h. autoscaler shows some OOM evictions on pods: "OOMKilled" on runtime-3 last 10m.
bob: pulling node metrics: node-12 memory pressure high, kube evict loop. Could be gradual memory leak or sudden traffic pattern.
eve: running quick tail logs for stalls:
```
# tail recent stall logs
kubectl logs runtime-3 -n prod --since=15m | grep -i stall | tail -n 50
# grep for KV load times > 50ms
kubectl logs runtime-3 -n prod --since=15m | jq -r '.msg | select(.kv_latency_ms > 50)'
```
alice: thanks. While infra investigates, let's do an immediate mitigation with traffic routing to a smaller quantized variant to reduce GPU memory/latency pressure. dave, can you cut 20% to small-quant?
dave: starting traffic shift. command:
```
redwoodctl route update --route "/v1/stream" --variant small-quant --weight 0.2
```
metrics-bot: Applied route update. Patch deployed to routing layer.
metrics-bot: 5m after reroute: p95 -> 1.1s, p99 -> 2.2s, request stalls decreased by ~62%. Throughput is stable.
alice: good improvement. That suggests heavier models were facing queueing. Keep the routing in place while we fix root cause.
bob: infra: isolating node-12, cordoning it to prevent further evictions. Looking at pod runtime-3 heap: process RSS trending upward. Dumping heap and starting memory profiler.
carol: runtime team: adding short-lived KV evict policy to bound active cache size as stop-gap. Config change applied: cache.max_entries = 5000 -> 3000.
eve: after cache cap, KV retrieval tail latency dropped ~45% on the runtime logs.
alice: Customer impact: CS flagged 3 enterprise orgs with elevated errors (ACME-inc, BrightHealth, Lumina). ACME webhooks showing 30% increase in timeouts. Notifying customer-success to open outreach.
bob: handing off incident commander to @bob. Alice -> passing IC to me while I keep infra workstream.
alice: handing off IC to bob. Logged handoff in incident doc. Bob, you're IC.
bob: I'm IC. Current mitigations: 1) 20% traffic -> small-quant (ongoing), 2) cordon node-12 + memory profiling, 3) cache cap applied. Next: evaluate rolling restart strategy for runtime pool to reclaim memory, coordinate with Dedicated customers for capacity.
dave: initiating rolling restart with maxUnavailable 1 to avoid big blast radius. command:
```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime -n prod --max-unavailable=1
```
metrics-bot: During rolling restart, watch p95 for regression. Will alert if p95 > 1.8s for 10m.
eve: quick grep shows a few application-level stack traces pointing to large prompt KV keys (very long conversation histories). We should throttle max conversation length on streaming route for now.
carol: queued a config change to reject conversations with prompt_length_tokens > 25k with a 429 + user-friendly message.
alice: good. Any sign of attacks or abnormal traffic shapes?
bob: traffic shape looks organic but a few clients are spiking with long sessions. CS will contact the customers for guidance.
metrics-bot: current numbers: p95 1.03s, p99 1.95s, error-rate back to baseline after routing. CPU and memory trending down post cordon and restart.
bob: IC notes: mitigation successful for now. We'll keep 20% small-quant in place until memory root cause is addressed. I'm going to create the incident doc and start the timeline + action items.
alice: thanks team. I'm un-assigning IC and going back to on-call standby.
bob: I will take IC. Assigning follow ups: infra to complete memory root cause (bob), runtime to harden cache eviction and add metrics (carol), product/CS to notify affected customers (alice -> cs).
dave: capturing commands and outputs in incident doc.
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-7642 — severity: S2 — tags: latency, streaming, p95/p99.
bob: adding postmortem template and prelim timeline. Will schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow and assign owners.
eve: leaving some quick remediation playbook snippets in doc: throttling long prompts, traffic routing to smaller variants, cordon nodes, rolling restarts.
alice: marking as transient mitigation achieved. Please keep this thread for live updates. If p95 creeps >1.5s again, page infra and IC. :white_check_mark:
